abstract: The success of foreign interventions critically depends on cohesion within local communities, which serve as relevant partners in counterinsurgency and reconstruction efforts. Using unique data on military base locations and counterinsurgency aid in Afghanistan, I show that the presence of the International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) negatively affects social cohesion, measured by support within communities, engagement with community institutions, and trust. I leverage a geographic regression discontinuity design to estimate effects of ISAF’s geographic mandate enlargement, complemented by a panel analysis that covers its operational intensification. These findings do not appear to reflect crowding-out of informal institutions by formal provision; rather, they coincide with higher insecurity and reduced confidence in local institutions, offering a plausible explanation for the observed erosion of community cohesion. These findings carry important implications for foreign policy, particularly in settings where communities compensate for gaps in formal institutional provision.
abstract_zh: 外国干预的成功关键取决于当地社区内部的凝聚力，这些社区在反叛乱和重建工作中是重要的合作伙伴。利用关于阿富汗军事基地位置和反叛乱援助的独特数据，我展示了国际安全援助部队（ISAF）的存在对社区凝聚力产生负面影响，这种凝聚力通过社区内部的支持、对社区机构的参与以及信任来衡量。我采用地理断点回归设计来估计ISAF地理任务扩大的效应，并辅以涵盖其行动强化的小组分析。这些发现似乎并未反映出正式供给对非正式机构的挤出效应；相反，它们与更高的不安全感和对地方机构信任度的降低相吻合，为观察到的社区凝聚力侵蚀提供了合理的解释。这些发现对外交政策具有重要意义，尤其是在社区弥补正式机构供给缺口的背景下。
title: Foreign interventions and community cohesion in times of conflict
title_zh: 冲突时期的外部干预与社区凝聚力

abstract: If public provision of public goods is potentially suboptimal, then why do states still intervene to provide them? This question parallels the broader inquiry into whether state provision can be explained without resorting to justifications invoking the public interest, or suboptimal private provision. This paper shows that whether states take over the provision of public goods depends on the political rents that can be secured in markets beyond the one for the public good itself. This creates a redistribution that is wide enough to secure sufficient buy-in from key interests (sustaining an equilibrium). Using the federalization of American lighthouses in the Early Republic (1789–1815) as a case study makes clear that this shift was not merely administrative. Rather, federal control was part of a rent-seeking arrangement that embedded subtle, yet significant, protectionist measures for the domestic shipping industry, created a broader “hidden tariff” often overlooked in economic history, and expanded patronage opportunities for political machines at both the state and federal levels. This example can be extended to other key historical episodes with implications for our understanding of the causes and consequences of state takeovers of the provision of public goods.
title: The takeover of public goods provision: Lighthouses in the Early American Republic
title_zh: 公共物品供给的接管：美国建国初期的灯塔

abstract: This paper develops a test for deciding whether latent systematic jumps in a large cross-section of asset prices obey a linear factor structure of low dimension. The test relies on a panel of high-frequency return observations for a large cross-section of assets over a fixed time interval. The latent systematic jumps are identified nonparametrically. The test is based on evaluating the statistical significance of the smallest eigenvalues of the outer product of the matrix of high-frequency increments that are identified to contain systematic jumps. The limit behavior of the test statistic, under the null hypothesis, is highly nonstandard, with systematic diffusive risks as well as idiosyncratic diffusive and jump risks in the asset prices all contributing to the limit in a distinct manner. An easy-to-implement bootstrap method is developed that allows for feasible implementation of the test. Empirical application to stocks in the S&P 500 index illustrates the usefulness of the proposed test.
title: The factor structure of jump risk

abstract: This paper investigates the impact of solar panel program announcements on household utility consumption. Using anonymized monthly block level electricity and water consumption data for each flat type from January 2011 to December 2020 in Singapore and a staggered difference-in-differences approach, we find that public housing buildings affected by the solar panel program tender announcements experience a 2.1% increase in monthly electricity consumption and a 2.3% increase in water consumption. We attribute this pattern to a financial misperception whereby households mistakenly believe that collective solar adoption will reduce their electricity costs, after ruling out alternative explanations such as changes in energy prices, wealth effects, and moral licensing. Our findings highlight the importance of effective information dissemination for the successful implementation of solar energy initiatives.
abstract_zh: 本文探讨了太阳能板项目公告对家庭公用事业消费的影响。利用2011年1月至2020年12月新加坡各户型每月匿名区块级电力与用水数据，并采用交错双重差分法，我们发现受太阳能板项目招标公告影响的公共住房建筑，其月度电力消费增加了2.1%，用水消费增加了2.3%。我们将这一现象归因于一种财务误解，即家庭错误地认为集体采用太阳能将降低其电费支出，在排除了能源价格变动、财富效应及道德许可等替代解释后，这一结论依然成立。我们的研究结果强调了有效信息传播对于太阳能倡议成功实施的重要性。
journal: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management
source_issue: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management, Volume 138
title: The illusion of free electricity: Household responses to solar panel program in Singapore
title_zh: 免费电力的幻觉：新加坡家庭对太阳能板项目的反应

abstract: Faster e-commerce fulfillment often comes at a cost to the environment because of energy-intensive transportation modes and more frequent, less consolidated last-mile deliveries. Despite these environmental implications, most retailers feel pressure to provide fast fulfillment to remain competitive. But what if consumers could be nudged to voluntarily choose green-but-slow shipping? In practice, a variety of information strategies are used to nudge such decisions, but it is unclear which strategy is best and why. This study examines these questions in two logistical contexts, each involving a different type of process change to support green-but-slow shipping: shipping mode and order consolidation. We first introduce a conceptual framework for selecting information strategies based on their influence on customer perceptions related to key stakeholders in each context: delivery convenience (self), environmental impact (society), and sustainability intention (retailer). Then, drawing on behavioral research and industry practices, we identify and test the effect of a comprehensive set of information strategies (i.e., Process, Green Label, Green Process, and Green Outcome) through controlled experiments involving 3,800 participants. Experimental results suggest that different logistical contexts require distinct nudging strategies, aligning with our conceptual framework. We find that including a green label is particularly effective for the shipping mode context, especially when combined with outcome information. In contrast, process information is more promising in the order consolidation context. Also, adding financial incentives can enhance the effectiveness of information strategies without a clear environmental signal, whereas pairing them with a simple green label may be effective for low eco-conscious individuals. This paper was accepted by Elena Katok, operations management. Funding: This work was supported by the Institute on the Environment, University of Minnesota [MF-0009-23]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.00239 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Nudging Green-but-Slow Shipping Choices in Online Retail
title_zh: 助推在线零售中的绿色但慢速配送选择

abstract: Assuming no arbitrage and that a polynomial in the time to maturity approximates spot-rate increments, we develop a consistent approach to estimate factor risk premia in the bond market. This approach is attractive, as the underlying risk factors are the time-varying coefficients of the polynomial specification, and the factor loadings correspond to familiar bond risk characteristics, such as duration and convexity. Our two-factor model—with a positive (negative) duration-factor (convexity-factor) risk premium—is easy to estimate and provides straightforward economic intuition for the concave term structure of bond risk premia and the downward-sloping term structure of bond Sharpe ratios. Our model decomposes the conditional factor risk premia into a “status quo” component—the expected factors’ realizations when expected spot-rate increments are zero—and the factors’ forecasts. The status quo factor risk premia provide measures of the state of fixed income markets that both outperform alternative measures and are easily estimated in real time; moreover, the underlying risk factors and their loadings are familiar to and readily interpreted by investors and traders. This paper was accepted by Lukas Schmid, finance. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.00212 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Bond Risk Characteristics and Factor Risk Premia
title_zh: 债券风险特征与因子风险溢价

abstract: We use a unique data set of individual housing transaction histories from Norway and a novel shift-share design to show that temporary changes in the transaction sequencing decisions of moving homeowners—whether to buy first and then sell or vice versa—cause temporary local increases in house prices and seller liquidity. Our findings are consistent with a simple theory of how transaction sequencing decisions impact house prices in a frictional housing market. We also provide the first causal estimate of the elasticity of house prices to market tightness, which is around 0.1. Overall, our findings highlight the importance of trading frictions and supply-demand imbalances for housing market dynamics. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. Funding: This work was supported by Norges Forskningsråd [Grant 274678: Frictions in the Housing Market]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.08149 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Transaction Sequencing and House Price Pressures

abstract: We study the role of gender in corporate debt renegotiation. Using in-court reorganizations from Brazil, we find that male-led creditors are more likely to reject plans put forward by female-led debtors. Although we cannot definitively identify the underlying mechanism driving this pattern, our findings align more consistently with gender-based discrimination compared with alternative explanations. This behavior may be costly: Female-led debtors deliver higher recoveries under reorganization than under liquidation, implying that rejections potentially create deadweight losses. Supporting a miscalibrated-beliefs explanation, we observe that the gender-based rejection gap narrows when male creditors have prior exposure to successful female-led businesses, pointing to a potential path for mitigation. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.05802 .
publisher: Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences (INFORMS)
title: Gender Gap in Debt Renegotiation
title_zh: 债务重新谈判中的性别差距

abstract: We find that the degree of extrapolative weighting in investors’ beliefs (DOX) has strong predictive power for a broad set of overreaction-related anomalies in the stock market. The average return spread of these anomalies is about [Formula: see text] per month following high DOX periods and [Formula: see text] per month following low DOX periods. In sharp contrast, DOX has opposite, but weaker, predictive power for underreaction-related anomalies. In addition, the predictive power of DOX is robust after controlling for a broad set of economic forces. Moreover, most of the DOX effect on long-short anomaly returns derives from the short legs of these overreaction-related anomalies, suggesting that time variation in DOX leads to more time variation in overpricing than in underpricing, probably because of short-sale impediments.
